<description>
Use CoinsViewOverlay to speed up ConnectBlock in TestBlockValidity. This also has the benefit of not inserting entries fetched from db into the main cache.

cs_main must be held for each place where the overlay is being used, and the reset guard ensures it will be reset for the next caller.
</description>

[2026-10-26] r:5649676670 review COMMENTED by Sjors (member) (edited 2026-10-26):
It would be good to add some relevant benchmarks in the PR description.

[quoted text omitted]
This might be useful regardless of the other change. Although `checkBlock()` is called by a (for now) trusted IPC client, that client in turn takes mostly untrusted data for miners. They could stuff our hot cache and trigger a flush.

At least one pool (DMND), which supports stratum v2 miner-provided templates, rate limits the number of blocks each client can check. But the more DoS-resistant we can make this, the better.

On the other hand, when validating many similar templates, it might be nice to actually insert fetched entries. But maybe, in a future optimization, the block template manager (#35675) could create a shared cache and opt-in to inserting fetched coins, up to a certain limit.

I changed the approach in https://github.com/Sjors/bitcoin/pull/122 a bit and updated the benchmarks.

It optimistically pre-fetch coins as the template is being assembled (see #35671). This gives it a head start in cases where at least one transaction is missing, when we have to wait a network roundtrip for the miner to provide it. I then added the approach from this PR on top; the optimistic sync is stopped and the coins it fetched are passed on to TestBlockValidity.

That approach does ~12ms of prep work during the network round-trip, but (so far) that implementation doesn't actually add any performance compared to this PR.

Update: with a 10 GB chainstate and a mostly cold cache, fetching from disk while waiting for the missing transactions can make a whole second difference in the final block check.
